title: Read one line at a time from a libevent bufferevent
summary: Swap chunk-by-chunk bufferevent_read for evbuffer_readln, and close the socket when the connection goes away.

turns.user: on_read is supposed to handle one command per line but sometimes a GET gets split into GE and T foo. only under load

assistant.body: Great catch! TCP is a stream of bytes with no idea where a line ends. bufferevent_read hands back whatever the input buffer holds at that moment, so a chunk boundary can land in the middle of a line. To read by line, take the evbuffer from bufferevent_get_input and pull lines out with evbuffer_readln. If no line ending has arrived yet it returns NULL, and the partial line stays in the buffer for the next callback. The line ending is EVBUFFER_EOL_CRLF_STRICT, which accepts both CRLF and a bare LF. Each line comes back malloc'd, so it is freed after use.

turns.user: typing into nc does nothing at all. telnet works

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. EVBUFFER_EOL_CRLF_STRICT accepts CRLF only. nc sends a bare LF on Enter, so no line ending was ever found. telnet sends CRLF, which is why it worked. The one that also takes a bare LF is EVBUFFER_EOL_CRLF.

turns.user: works. but after a day accept dies with Too many open files. im freeing on disconnect, pretty sure

assistant.body: bufferevent_free frees the bufferevent and nothing else. It does not close the socket. To have it closed as well, pass BEV_OPT_CLOSE_ON_FREE when creating it. The options are 0 right now, so every disconnect left one fd behind.

turns.user: also what if someone just streams forever without a newline, cant they eat all the memory?

assistant.body: Exactly right. Until a line ending arrives, evbuffer_readln takes nothing out, so the input buffer grows without bound. After handling every complete line, check what is left with evbuffer_get_length and drop the connection past a limit. Note: libevent holds a reference to the bufferevent for the length of the callback, so calling bufferevent_free in here only frees it after the callback returns. With CLOSE_ON_FREE set, the socket closes along with it.
